title: Bake and measure
author: claude
summary: We baked the evening room and compared it with the day room.
what: We baked the evening room and measured it against the day room.
why: To check that the evening is not over-bright and that nothing clips.
how:
- The `mood=evening` setting runs through all the pipeline scripts and the new `run_evening.sh`.
- Blender bakes at 1024 samples.
- Evening light maps are stored at half brightness, so bright spots do not clip (the day uses a quarter).
- The probe keeps more of the lamps' warm colour than the day probe does.

Results:
- The evening file is 11.6 MB.
- Compared with the day, the floor gets 69% of the light, the walls 83 to 91%, and the ceiling 96%.
- Only the lamp stem is brighter than the picture format can hold.
- The evening probe is darker than the day probe.

tech.name: Cycles
tech.plain: Blender's realistic renderer. It follows light the way a camera would see it.

tech.name: Baking
tech.plain: Calculating the light once, in advance, and saving the result as pictures.

tech.name: Light maps
tech.plain: Pictures of how bright each surface is, laid over the walls and floor so the browser does not have to calculate light.

tech.name: 360-degree probe
tech.plain: A panorama of the room taken from the table. It lights and reflects in the table and chairs.
